Просить у кого. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'довольствие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'pleasure' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Даже Лёша начал ходить в садик с удовольствием.
examples.trans: Even Lyosha started going to daycare with pleasure.

meanings.note: Утром = in the morning. Common neuter noun meaning 'morning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: instrumental of утро used as an adverb

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'owner', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The restaurant owner personally greets the guests.
The owner is busy in the kitchen for now.

examples.text: Вовсе нет, я жду хозяина ресторана.
examples.trans: Not at all, I am waiting for the restaurant owner.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
Common neuter noun meaning 'egg' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It is time to add the eggs.

examples.text: Макс, быстрее! Уже пора добавлять яйца.
examples.trans: Max, faster! It is time to add the eggs.

examples.text: Берём свежие яйца и разогреваем сковороду.
examples.trans: We take fresh eggs and heat the frying pan.
